subject: maths
title: The Mean
seo_title: Year 6 Mean Worksheets: Find the Mean, Missing Values and Bar Charts (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Calculate and interpret the mean as an average.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 maths worksheets on the mean: share equally, find the mean of whole numbers, decimals and money, read it from bar charts and tables, work out a missing value, and solve SATs-style word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_sub: The mean is what each value would be if the total were shared out equally. Count every value, including 0. To work backwards, total = mean × number of values.
body_html:
What is the mean?

The mean is a kind of average. It tells you what each value would be if the total were shared out equally.

Mean = total ÷ number of values

Example 1

Find the mean of 12, 8, 15, 9 and 11.

Total: 12 + 8 + 15 + 9 + 11 = 55. There are 5 numbers. 55 ÷ 5 = 11.

Answer: 11

When the mean is a decimal

The mean does not have to be a whole number, and it does not have to be one of the values.

Example 2

Four children are 136 cm, 142 cm, 139 cm and 145 cm tall. What is their mean height?

Total: 136 + 142 + 139 + 145 = 562. 562 ÷ 4 = 140.5.

Answer: 140.5 cm

Example 3

Four drinks cost £2.40, £1.85, £3.20 and £1.75. What is the mean cost?

Total: £2.40 + £1.85 + £3.20 + £1.75 = £9.20. £9.20 ÷ 4 = £2.30.

Answer: £2.30

The mean from a bar chart

Read every bar, add them, then divide by the number of bars. A bar of 0 still counts.

Work backwards from the mean

If you know the mean, you can find the total: total = mean × number of values. This helps you find a missing value.

Example 4

The mean of 5 numbers is 12. Four of the numbers are 10, 15, 9 and 14. What is the fifth number?

Total of all 5: 5 × 12 = 60. The four numbers add to 10 + 15 + 9 + 14 = 48. 60 − 48 = 12.

Answer: 12

Example 5

Isla’s first 3 test scores are 16, 13 and 17. What must she score in the 4th test to have a mean of 16?

Total needed: 4 × 16 = 64. So far: 16 + 13 + 17 = 46. 64 − 46 = 18.

Answer: 18

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Forgetting to count a 0 (a match with no goals)A 0 is a value: count it when you divide
Dividing by the wrong numberDivide by how many values there are
Leaving out a value when addingTick each value as you add it
Choosing the middle value of the listThe mean is total ÷ number of values
Giving the total as the answerRemember to divide
Dividing the mean by the count to find the totalTotal = mean × number of values
Averaging two means for groups of different sizesFind each total, add them, then divide by everyone

faq.q: How do you find the mean in Year 6?
faq.a: Add all the values to find the total, then divide by how many values there are. For 4, 7, 6 and 3 the total is 20, and 20 ÷ 4 = 5, so the mean is 5.

faq.q: Is the mean in the Year 6 maths SATs?
faq.a: Yes. Calculating and interpreting the mean is part of the Year 6 statistics curriculum, so it can come up in the reasoning papers, often with a table or bar chart or as a missing-value problem.

faq.q: How do you find a missing number when you know the mean?
faq.a: Multiply the mean by the number of values to get the total. Then subtract the numbers you know. If the mean of 4 numbers is 10 and three are 8, 12 and 9, the missing number is 40 − 29 = 11.

faq.q: What is the difference between the mean, median and mode?
faq.a: The mean shares the total out equally. The median is the middle value and the mode is the most common value; in England these are taught from Year 7, while Year 6 focuses on the mean.

items.q: Cubes are moved between these 3 towers until all the towers are the same height. How many cubes are in each tower now? (This is the mean.)
items.e: Total cubes: 8 + 9 + 1 = 18. Share them equally between 3 towers: 18 ÷ 3 = 6 cubes each.

items.q: Cubes are moved between these 4 towers until all the towers are the same height. How many cubes are in each tower now? (This is the mean.)
items.e: Total cubes: 2 + 7 + 3 + 4 = 16. Share them equally between 4 towers: 16 ÷ 4 = 4 cubes each.

items.q: Cubes are moved between these 3 towers until all the towers are the same height. How many cubes are in each tower now? (This is the mean.)
items.e: Total cubes: 8 + 3 + 4 = 15. Share them equally between 3 towers: 15 ÷ 3 = 5 cubes each.

items.q: Cubes are moved between these 4 towers until all the towers are the same height. How many cubes are in each tower now? (This is the mean.)
items.e: Total cubes: 3 + 8 + 6 + 3 = 20. Share them equally between 4 towers: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cubes each.

items.q: Cubes are moved between these 5 towers until all the towers are the same height. How many cubes are in each tower now? (This is the mean.)
items.e: Total cubes: 9 + 1 + 7 + 8 + 5 = 30. Share them equally between 5 towers: 30 ÷ 5 = 6 cubes each.

items.q: Cubes are moved between these 4 towers until all the towers are the same height. How many cubes are in each tower now? (This is the mean.)
items.e: Total cubes: 7 + 8 + 4 + 1 = 20. Share them equally between 4 towers: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cubes each.

items.q: Ruby did these numbers of keepy-uppies in 4 tries: 7, 16, 21 and 24. What is the mean?
items.e: Total: 7 + 16 + 21 + 24 = 68. There are 4 values, so divide by 4: 68 ÷ 4 = 17.

items.q: The numbers of packets of crisps sold at the tuck shop on 5 days were 19, 9, 22, 16 and 19. What is the mean?
items.e: Total: 19 + 9 + 22 + 16 + 19 = 85. There are 5 values, so divide by 5: 85 ÷ 5 = 17.

items.q: Oliver got these marks in 6 spelling tests, out of 10: 3, 3, 10, 7, 9 and 4. What is the mean?
items.e: Total: 3 + 3 + 10 + 7 + 9 + 4 = 36. There are 6 values, so divide by 6: 36 ÷ 6 = 6.

items.q: The numbers of sweets in 6 party bags are 6, 9, 9, 15, 12 and 9. What is the mean?
items.e: Total: 6 + 9 + 9 + 15 + 12 + 9 = 60. There are 6 values, so divide by 6: 60 ÷ 6 = 10.

items.q: Charlie scored these numbers of runs in 6 games of cricket: 2, 14, 11, 0, 11 and 16. What is the mean?
items.e: Total: 2 + 14 + 11 + 0 + 11 + 16 = 54. There are 6 values (count the 0 too), so divide by 6: 54 ÷ 6 = 9.

items.q: The numbers of goals a football team scored in 4 matches were 5, 3, 0 and 4. What is the mean?
items.e: Total: 5 + 3 + 0 + 4 = 12. There are 4 values (count the 0 too), so divide by 4: 12 ÷ 4 = 3.

items.q: George read these numbers of pages on 6 nights: 23, 11, 21, 8, 15 and 12. What is the mean?
items.e: Total: 23 + 11 + 21 + 8 + 15 + 12 = 90. There are 6 values, so divide by 6: 90 ÷ 6 = 15.

items.q: The numbers of lorries that passed the school in 6 lessons were 1, 4, 0, 5, 7 and 7. What is the mean?
items.e: Total: 1 + 4 + 0 + 5 + 7 + 7 = 24. There are 6 values (count the 0 too), so divide by 6: 24 ÷ 6 = 4.

items.q: The heights, in cm, of 4 sunflower seedlings are 14, 8, 12 and 14. What is the mean?
items.e: Total: 14 + 8 + 12 + 14 = 48. There are 4 values, so divide by 4: 48 ÷ 4 = 12.

items.q: The numbers of pupils absent from Year 6 on 5 days were 1, 3, 5, 0 and 1. What is the mean?
items.e: Total: 1 + 3 + 5 + 0 + 1 = 10. There are 5 values (count the 0 too), so divide by 5: 10 ÷ 5 = 2.

items.q: The numbers of children at after-school club on 5 days were 22, 19, 10, 10 and 19. What is the mean?
items.e: Total: 22 + 19 + 10 + 10 + 19 = 80. There are 5 values, so divide by 5: 80 ÷ 5 = 16.

items.q: The ages, in years, of 5 children at a party are 9, 11, 6, 9 and 5. What is the mean?
items.e: Total: 9 + 11 + 6 + 9 + 5 = 40. There are 5 values, so divide by 5: 40 ÷ 5 = 8.

items.q: Jack counted the birds in the garden on 6 mornings: 7, 5, 8, 12, 10 and 6. What is the mean?
items.e: Total: 7 + 5 + 8 + 12 + 10 + 6 = 48. There are 6 values, so divide by 6: 48 ÷ 6 = 8.

items.q: Isla’s house team scored these points in 4 quizzes: 4, 14, 9 and 5. What is the mean?
items.e: Total: 4 + 14 + 9 + 5 = 32. There are 4 values, so divide by 4: 32 ÷ 4 = 8.

items.q: The heights of 4 children in Year 6 are 149, 137, 153 and 132 cm. What is their mean height?
items.e: Total: 149 + 137 + 153 + 132 = 571. There are 4 values, so divide by 4: 571 ÷ 4 = 142.75 cm.

items.q: The numbers of visitors to a museum on 4 days were 2,304, 1,333, 2,134 and 1,873. What was the mean number of visitors per day?
Grace’s long jumps were 2.59, 2.77, 2.94 and 2.90 m. What was her mean jump?
Alfie scored 43, 60, 55 and 55 in 4 games of darts. What was his mean score?
items.e: Total: 43 + 60 + 55 + 55 = 213. There are 4 values, so divide by 4: 213 ÷ 4 = 53.25.

items.q: A school counted the steps pupils walked in 5 lunchtimes: 2,364, 2,472, 2,648, 3,093 and 2,193. What is the mean?
The numbers of pupils in 3 classes are 29, 30 and 24. What is the mean, to 1 decimal place?
items.e: Total: 29 + 30 + 24 = 83. Divide by 3: 83 ÷ 3 = 27.667… Round to 1 decimal place: 27.7.

items.q: A farmer’s 5 hens laid 18, 21, 22, 24 and 21 eggs in a month. What is the mean number of eggs per hen?
items.e: Total: 18 + 21 + 22 + 24 + 21 = 106. There are 5 values, so divide by 5: 106 ÷ 5 = 21.2.

items.q: A rain gauge collected 9.6, 3.5, 8.7, 6.2 and 3.4 mm of rain on 5 days. What was the mean daily rainfall?
items.e: Total: 9.6 + 3.5 + 8.7 + 6.2 + 3.4 = 31.4. There are 5 values, so divide by 5: 31.4 ÷ 5 = 6.28 mm.

items.q: Oliver bought 4 drinks costing £1.55, 70p, £1.30 and £1.25. What was the mean cost of a drink?
The crowds at 3 rugby matches were 2,942, 6,708 and 4,336. What was the mean crowd?
Amelia scored 19, 20, 19, 18, 19 and 17 on 6 times-tables tests. What is the mean, to 1 decimal place?
items.e: Total: 19 + 20 + 19 + 18 + 19 + 17 = 112. Divide by 6: 112 ÷ 6 = 18.667… Round to 1 decimal place: 18.7.

items.q: The masses of 8 pumpkins are 12, 11, 7, 12, 3, 4, 10 and 7 kg. What is their mean mass?
items.e: Total: 12 + 11 + 7 + 12 + 3 + 4 + 10 + 7 = 66. There are 8 values, so divide by 8: 66 ÷ 8 = 8.25 kg.

items.q: The prices of 5 paperback books are £7.95, £6.15, £8.75, £4.85 and £3.95. What is the mean price?
Five parcels have masses of 3.4, 1.3, 3.9, 3.0 and 2.9 kg. What is their mean mass?
items.e: Total: 3.4 + 1.3 + 3.9 + 3.0 + 2.9 = 14.5. There are 5 values, so divide by 5: 14.5 ÷ 5 = 2.9 kg.

items.q: Ethan ran 60 m four times. He took 11.5, 11.6, 10.3 and 10.0 seconds. What was his mean time?
items.e: Total: 11.5 + 11.6 + 10.3 + 10.0 = 43.4. There are 4 values, so divide by 4: 43.4 ÷ 4 = 10.85 s.

items.q: The numbers of cars in the car park on 7 days were 52, 55, 34, 40, 70, 54 and 42. What is the mean, to 1 decimal place?
Charlie spent £2.80, £3.05, £3.80, £3.40 and £3.30 on lunch on 5 school days. What was the mean amount per day?
The numbers of books borrowed from the library on 6 days were 20, 12, 39, 27, 38 and 21. What is the mean, to 1 decimal place?
items.e: Total: 20 + 12 + 39 + 27 + 38 + 21 = 157. Divide by 6: 157 ÷ 6 = 26.167… Round to 1 decimal place: 26.2.

items.q: Four pupils raised £17.70, £16.15, £14.95 and £7.00 for charity. What was the mean amount raised?
The costs of 3 cinema tickets were £8.85, £10.60 and £9.35. What was the mean cost?

sets.title: Mean from a bar chart or table

items.q: What was the mean number of goals per match?
items.e: Total: 0 + 3 + 5 + 4 + 2 + 4 = 18. There are 6 matches (count the 0 too), so divide by 6: 18 ÷ 6 = 3.

items.q: What is the mean distance?
items.e: Total: 2.7 + 2.3 + 3.5 + 4.3 = 12.8. There are 4 pupils, so divide by 4: 12.8 ÷ 4 = 3.2 km.

items.q: What was the mean number of points per house?
items.e: Total: 20 + 20 + 40 + 70 = 150. There are 4 houses, so divide by 4: 150 ÷ 4 = 37.5.

items.q: What is the mean amount raised?
items.e: Total: £40 + £159 + £119 + £87 = £405. There are 4 classes, so divide by 4: £405 ÷ 4 = £101.25.

items.q: What was the mean daily rainfall?
items.e: Total: 12 + 16 + 6 + 0 + 6 = 40. There are 5 days (count the 0 too), so divide by 5: 40 ÷ 5 = 8 mm.

items.q: What is the mean mass?
On how many days was the number of cakes greater than the mean?
items.e: Mean: 150 ÷ 5 = 30. Bars above 30: Wednesday, Thursday. So the answer is 2.

items.q: What was the mean number of cakes sold per day?
items.e: Total: 25 + 25 + 25 + 20 + 10 = 105. There are 5 days, so divide by 5: 105 ÷ 5 = 21.

items.q: What is the mean number of bottles per class?
items.e: Total: 36 + 37 + 79 + 63 + 72 = 287. There are 5 classes, so divide by 5: 287 ÷ 5 = 57.4.

items.q: What was the mean number of books read per pupil?
items.e: Total: 16 + 2 + 2 + 4 + 6 = 30. There are 5 pupils, so divide by 5: 30 ÷ 5 = 6.

items.q: What is the mean highest temperature?
items.e: Total: 17 + 23 + 18 + 18 + 16 = 92. There are 5 days, so divide by 5: 92 ÷ 5 = 18.4 °C.

items.q: The bar for Blue is missing. The mean is 45 points per house. What should the missing bar show?
items.e: Total = mean × number of bars = 45 × 4 = 180. The other bars add to 30 + 40 + 50 = 120. Missing bar: 180 − 120 = 60.

items.q: What was the mean number of runs per over?
items.e: Total: 0 + 2 + 5 + 3 + 2 + 9 = 21. There are 6 overs (count the 0 too), so divide by 6: 21 ÷ 6 = 3.5.

items.q: What is the mean time?
items.e: Total: 15.8 + 18.1 + 16.9 + 19.6 = 70.4. There are 4 pupils, so divide by 4: 70.4 ÷ 4 = 17.6 s.

items.q: What was the mean number of pupils in the library per day?
items.e: Total: 15 + 30 + 40 + 25 + 35 = 145. There are 5 days, so divide by 5: 145 ÷ 5 = 29.

items.q: What is the mean monthly rainfall?
items.e: Total: 72 + 41 + 63 + 86 + 48 + 32 = 342. There are 6 months, so divide by 6: 342 ÷ 6 = 57 mm.

items.q: On how many days was the number of pupils greater than the mean?
items.e: Mean: 70 ÷ 5 = 14. Bars above 14: Monday, Friday. So the answer is 2.

items.q: What was the mean number of hours of sunshine per day?
items.e: Total: 8 + 9 + 3 + 3 + 0 + 3 + 9 = 35. There are 7 days (count the 0 too), so divide by 7: 35 ÷ 7 = 5.

items.q: What is the mean number of pupils absent per day?
items.e: Total: 4 + 5 + 3 + 4 + 0 = 16. There are 5 days (count the 0 too), so divide by 5: 16 ÷ 5 = 3.2.

items.q: The bar for Noah is missing. The mean is 12 books per pupil. What should the missing bar show?
items.e: Total = mean × number of bars = 12 × 5 = 60. The other bars add to 16 + 8 + 14 + 16 = 54. Missing bar: 60 − 54 = 6.

sets.title: Find the total or a missing value

items.q: The mean of 8 numbers is 11. What is the total of the 8 numbers?
items.e: Mean = total ÷ number of values, so total = mean × number of values: 11 × 8 = 88.

items.q: The mean of 4 numbers is 27. Three of the numbers are 35, 21 and 19. What is the other number?
items.e: Total of all 4 numbers: 4 × 27 = 108. Known numbers: 35 + 21 + 19 = 75. Missing number: 108 − 75 = 33.

items.q: The mean mass of 6 parcels is 4.1 kg. What is their total mass?
items.e: Mean = total ÷ number of values, so total = mean × number of values: 4.1 × 6 = 24.6 kg.

items.q: The mean of 5 numbers is 27. Four of the numbers are 28, 26, 21 and 19. What is the other number?
items.e: Total of all 5 numbers: 5 × 27 = 135. Known numbers: 28 + 26 + 21 + 19 = 94. Missing number: 135 − 94 = 41.

items.q: Freya scored a mean of 16 marks in 8 tests. How many marks did she score altogether?
items.e: Mean = total ÷ number of values, so total = mean × number of values: 16 × 8 = 128.

items.q: The mean of 5 numbers is 18. Four of the numbers are 14, 9, 18 and 14. What is the other number?
items.e: Total of all 5 numbers: 5 × 18 = 90. Known numbers: 14 + 9 + 18 + 14 = 55. Missing number: 90 − 55 = 35.

items.q: The mean of 3 numbers is 16. The number 36 is added. What is the mean of all 4 numbers now?
items.e: Old total: 16 × 3 = 48. New total: 48 + 36 = 84. New mean: 84 ÷ 4 = 21.

items.q: The mean length of 6 ribbons is 7.2 cm. What is their total length?
items.e: Mean = total ÷ number of values, so total = mean × number of values: 7.2 × 6 = 43.2 cm.

items.q: The mean of 6 numbers is 26. Five of the numbers are 27, 20, 19, 19 and 24. What is the other number?
items.e: Total of all 6 numbers: 6 × 26 = 156. Known numbers: 27 + 20 + 19 + 19 + 24 = 109. Missing number: 156 − 109 = 47.

items.q: The mean of 4 numbers is 7. The number 27 is added. What is the mean of all 5 numbers now?
items.e: Old total: 7 × 4 = 28. New total: 28 + 27 = 55. New mean: 55 ÷ 5 = 11.

items.q: The mean of 4 numbers is 13. What is the sum of the numbers?
items.e: Mean = total ÷ number of values, so total = mean × number of values: 13 × 4 = 52.

items.q: The mean of 4 numbers is 30. Three of the numbers are 29, 22 and 36. What is the other number?
items.e: Total of all 4 numbers: 4 × 30 = 120. Known numbers: 29 + 22 + 36 = 87. Missing number: 120 − 87 = 33.

items.q: The mean of 5 numbers is 10. The number 34 is added. What is the mean of all 6 numbers now?
items.e: Old total: 10 × 5 = 50. New total: 50 + 34 = 84. New mean: 84 ÷ 6 = 14.

items.q: The mean of 5 numbers is 14. One of the numbers, 2, is removed. What is the mean of the other 4 numbers?
items.e: Old total: 14 × 5 = 70. Take away 2: 70 − 2 = 68. New mean: 68 ÷ 4 = 17.

items.q: The mean of 5 numbers is 38. Four of the numbers are 30, 29, 31 and 40. What is the other number?
items.e: Total of all 5 numbers: 5 × 38 = 190. Known numbers: 30 + 29 + 31 + 40 = 130. Missing number: 190 − 130 = 60.

items.q: The mean of 4 numbers is 20. The number 10 is added. What is the mean of all 5 numbers now?
items.e: Old total: 20 × 4 = 80. New total: 80 + 10 = 90. New mean: 90 ÷ 5 = 18.

items.q: Jack’s mean score in 5 spelling tests (out of 20) was 13. Then his teacher found a mistake: one score of 6 should have been 16. What is the correct mean?
items.e: The total goes up by 16 − 6 = 10. Shared between 5 tests, the mean goes up by 10 ÷ 5 = 2. Correct mean: 13 + 2 = 15.

items.q: The mean of 6 numbers is 55. Five of the numbers are 54, 49, 63, 47 and 47. What is the other number?
items.e: Total of all 6 numbers: 6 × 55 = 330. Known numbers: 54 + 49 + 63 + 47 + 47 = 260. Missing number: 330 − 260 = 70.

items.q: The mean of 5 numbers is 19. One of the numbers, 31, is removed. What is the mean of the other 4 numbers?
items.e: Old total: 19 × 5 = 95. Take away 31: 95 − 31 = 64. New mean: 64 ÷ 4 = 16.

items.q: Isla’s mean score in 5 spelling tests (out of 20) was 9. Then her teacher found a mistake: one score of 3 should have been 13. What is the correct mean?
items.e: The total goes up by 13 − 3 = 10. Shared between 5 tests, the mean goes up by 10 ÷ 5 = 2. Correct mean: 9 + 2 = 11.

items.q: The school football team scored 2, 0, 4, 1, 4 and 1 goals in its last 6 matches. What was the mean number of goals per match?
items.e: Total: 2 + 0 + 4 + 1 + 4 + 1 = 12. There are 6 matches (count the 0 too), so divide by 6: 12 ÷ 6 = 2.

items.q: Aisha’s scores on 3 spelling tests (out of 20) were 18, 13 and 17. What does she need to score on the next one to have a mean of 15?
items.e: For a mean of 15 over 4 tests, the total must be 4 × 15 = 60. So far: 18 + 13 + 17 = 48. Aisha needs 60 − 48 = 12.

items.q: In a quiz, the 4 Hawks scored 5, 12, 14 and 13 points and the 6 Falcons scored 11, 5, 7, 13, 5 and 7 points. How much greater is the Hawks’ mean score than the Falcons’?
items.e: Hawks: 44 ÷ 4 = 11. Falcons: 48 ÷ 6 = 8. Difference: 11 − 8 = 3. (The Falcons have the greater total, but they have more players, so compare the means.)

items.q: The highest temperatures in Brighton during one week in July were 15, 26, 24, 27, 20, 19 and 23 °C. What was the mean highest temperature?
items.e: Total: 15 + 26 + 24 + 27 + 20 + 19 + 23 = 154. There are 7 days, so divide by 7: 154 ÷ 7 = 22 °C.

items.q: In a reading challenge, 4 pupils in Year 5 read a mean of 9 books each and 8 pupils in Year 6 read a mean of 6 books each. What was the mean for all 12 pupils?
items.e: Totals: 4 × 9 = 36 and 8 × 6 = 48. All together: 84 books for 12 pupils. Mean: 84 ÷ 12 = 7. (Do not just find the mean of 9 and 6: the groups are different sizes.)

items.q: A school has 4 classes with a mean of 27 pupils per class. A new class of 22 pupils joins the school. What is the new mean number of pupils per class?
items.e: Pupils before: 4 × 27 = 108. Now: 108 + 22 = 130 pupils in 5 classes. New mean: 130 ÷ 5 = 26.

items.q: The mean mass of 3 bags of flour is 1.9 kg. What is the total mass of the 3 bags?
items.e: Total = mean × number of bags = 1.9 × 3 = 5.7 kg.

items.q: Noah swam a length of the pool 4 times. His times were 21.9, 22.8, 16.1 and 15.4 seconds. What was his mean time?
items.e: Total: 21.9 + 22.8 + 16.1 + 15.4 = 76.2. There are 4 lengths, so divide by 4: 76.2 ÷ 4 = 19.05 s.

items.q: The temperatures at 8 am on 5 winter mornings were 3, 4, −1, −1 and 5 °C. What was the mean temperature?
items.e: Total: 3 + 4 − 1 − 1 + 5 = 10. There are 5 mornings, so divide by 5: 10 ÷ 5 = 2 °C. (Remember: adding a negative number is the same as subtracting.)

items.q: At the tuck shop, Grace bought 4 snacks costing £1.40, £1.35, £1.25 and £1.60. What was the mean cost of a snack?
In a quiz, the 4 Robins scored 17, 19, 25 and 23 points and the 6 Owls scored 24, 22, 25, 12, 21 and 10 points. How much greater is the Robins’ mean score than the Owls’?
items.e: Robins: 84 ÷ 4 = 21. Owls: 114 ÷ 6 = 19. Difference: 21 − 19 = 2. (The Owls have the greater total, but they have more players, so compare the means.)

items.q: The rainfall in Manchester each day for a week was 14, 6, 0, 0, 0, 3 and 5 mm. What was the mean daily rainfall?
items.e: Total: 14 + 6 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 3 + 5 = 28. There are 7 days (count the 0 too), so divide by 7: 28 ÷ 7 = 4 mm.

items.q: Zara’s scores on 4 arithmetic practice papers (out of 40) were 32, 36, 31 and 35. What does she need to score on the next one to have a mean of 34?
items.e: For a mean of 34 over 5 papers, the total must be 5 × 34 = 170. So far: 32 + 36 + 31 + 35 = 134. Zara needs 170 − 134 = 36.

items.q: The mean age of 4 children is 11 years. When their teacher joins them, the mean age of all 5 people is 14 years. How old is the teacher?
items.e: Children’s total: 4 × 11 = 44. Total with the teacher: 5 × 14 = 70. Teacher: 70 − 44 = 26 years.

items.q: Four Year 6 classes held a cake sale. They raised £590, £410, £360 and £390. What was the mean amount raised per class?
Year 6 grew 5 bean plants. After 3 weeks their heights were 16.0, 15.8, 8.9, 10.7 and 10.1 cm. What was the mean height?
The school football team scored 0, 2, 3, 1, 0, 4, 1 and 1 goals in its last 8 matches. What was the mean number of goals per match?
items.e: Total: 0 + 2 + 3 + 1 + 0 + 4 + 1 + 1 = 12. There are 8 matches (count the 0 too), so divide by 8: 12 ÷ 8 = 1.5.

items.q: Kai’s mean score in 3 games was 12. Ethan’s mean score in 4 games was 10. Who scored more points in total, and how many more?
items.e: Kai: 12 × 3 = 36 points. Ethan: 10 × 4 = 40 points. Ethan scored 40 − 36 = 4 more. A higher mean does not always mean a higher total.

items.q: Alfie’s scores on 2 reasoning practice papers (out of 35) were 31 and 23. What does he need to score on the next one to have a mean of 28?
items.e: For a mean of 28 over 3 papers, the total must be 3 × 28 = 84. So far: 31 + 23 = 54. Alfie needs 84 − 54 = 30.

items.q: Arjun cycled a mean distance of 4.5 km a day for 6 days. How far did he cycle altogether?
items.e: Total = mean × number of days = 4.5 × 6 = 27 km.
